question.text: What is the suitability and appropriateness framework that applies to interest rate derivative contracts?

answer.text: IRD contracts are subject to the RBI suitability and appropriateness (S&A) policy and exchange/member risk-disclosure requirements
Users must pass a mandatory test before being allowed to trade IRDs
SEBI rates each IRD product on a risk scale and users choose accordingly
Banks must provide a guarantee for all user positions in IRD

explanation.text: The Logic: Derivative contracts are subject to the RBI suitability and appropriateness policy, and FIMMDA's code addresses S&A standards. Exchanges and their members are required to ensure that clients are made aware of the risks of trading derivative contracts, including risk disclosure in light of the client's financial condition. The Trap: There is no mandatory user test, no SEBI product risk-rating scale, and no general bank guarantee for user positions in this framework. Note: The S&A policy and exchange/member risk-disclosure rules together provide the suitability framework; do not overstate it as a detailed market-maker user-profiling regime.
